transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I know my paintings have an important message for the people running this country, and no one seems to understand that. My wife and friends keep telling me it's far-fetched, but I know it's absolutely true. I just need someone to actually listen and see what is going on.
Have you recently felt a decreased need for sleep, or felt unusually energetic and active while working on these paintings?

Oh, absolutely, I have an immense amount of energy and have been staying up incredibly late in my workshop sketching and repainting canvases. I've been completely neglecting sleep because I feel this restless drive to keep moving, reorganizing things, and working on my art. I just can't sit still or rest right now because there is so much to do.
Have you ever had these strong beliefs about your paintings or other unusual experiences during times when your energy levels were completely normal and you weren't feeling this intense drive?

No, I've never had these ideas about my art or heard my brother's voice when my energy was normal. It all only started when I got so wound up and driven over the last couple of months. On the rare days when my energy dips back to normal, those thoughts and voices seem to fade into the background.
Have you ever had periods in the past where you felt the exact opposite—very down, sad, or hopeless—or other times when you felt this high and energetic?

No, I don't recall ever having extreme ups or downs like this in the past. I've never felt that kind of deep sadness, nor have I ever felt this incredibly wound up before. This is really the first time anything like this has happened to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-lifetime episode of mania characterized by severely increased energy, decreased need for sleep, psychomotor agitation, and goal-directed hyperactivity lasting for a couple of months. This is accompanied by congruent psychotic features, including grandiose delusions regarding the national importance of his paintings and auditory hallucinations (hearing his brother's voice). These psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the manic state. Since there is no history of prior mood episodes, a single manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
